name: Checking Claims Against the Ledger
title: Checking Claims Against the Ledger
answer: Checking claims against the ledger means comparing public sustainability and carbon statements, such as net zero pledges or emissions reductions, with the underlying accounting records and transactional data that support them. It covers voluntary disclosures, regulatory filings, and supplier or product-level claims. The work sits within carbon accounting because the ledger is the source of truth for energy use, offsets, allowances, and capital expenditure. Practitioners look for gaps between what a company says and what its books show.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Checking claims against the ledger means comparing public sustainability and carbon statements, such as net zero pledges or emissions reductions, with the underlying accounting records and transactional data that support them. It covers voluntary disclosures, regulatory filings, and supplier or product-level claims. The work sits within carbon accounting because the ledger is the source of truth for energy use, offsets, allowances, and capital expenditure. Practitioners look for gaps between what a company says and what its books show.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: This runs on the same systems used for financial audit and carbon inventory: ERP ledgers, energy and fuel procurement records, emissions factor databases, and document repositories for filings and press releases. AI tools for this task typically connect to structured ledger exports, utility invoices, and unstructured text in sustainability reports. The site's tracked company pages and compliance pages provide a reference set for where claims and ledger data meet. No special hardware is required beyond normal cloud or on-premise data processing.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by extracting claims from text, mapping them to ledger accounts and cost centers, and testing whether the numbers reconcile. Natural language processing identifies quantitative promises, while rules and statistical checks compare them against recorded energy spend, offset purchases, and capital projects. Where a claim cannot be traced to a ledger entry, it is flagged for human review. The goal is not to judge intent but to show whether the accounting supports the statement.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on access to financial records, confidentiality, and the accuracy of automated flags. A false finding can damage a company or mislead regulators, so outputs are treated as audit evidence rather than conclusions. Provenance matters: every comparison should record which ledger extract, filing, and model version was used. This page describes practice, not legal advice, and users should follow their own audit standards and data-sharing agreements.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The practice is moving toward continuous assurance, where claims are checked against ledger feeds as soon as they are published. AI is also being used to compare claims across subsidiaries and supply chains, not just at group level. As carbon accounting standards tighten, the ledger will need to carry more granular emissions data, making automated reconciliation more feasible. Expect closer links between financial audit and sustainability assurance.
